## Carry-forward for the next batch: digithings #6016

This is the PR author's factual update, not a review.

- **PR** digithings #6016 - https://github.com/digithings-ai/digithings/pull/6016
  ("fix(digichat): one source for the session lock and the model allowlist")
- **Head** `f0335113a383a27a6b90d36420d6bbe1a80be143`, base `develop`, not a draft
- **Leaf** DIG-4589, `in_review`, assigned to the Software Architect seat
- **Merge state** `mergeable: true`; `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED` (the review
  leg, not a conflict - the branch was rebased on `develop` and is clean)
- **CI on this head** the GitHub rows are running (Analyze in progress,
  CodeQL and Supabase Preview as before). The `local-ci` and `review-applied`
  rows are not a verdict: the host disk guard skips the tick while
  `~/.config/digithings/state/worktree-pause` exists, and that file is stale
  (it records 70 GB free, the data volume shows 166 GiB free). Local evidence
  on this head: digichat suite 175 files / 2041 tests / 0 failed, `tsc
  --noEmit` clean, eslint clean on the six changed code files.

**What this PR needs from the batch.** The two in-session reviews on it (QA
Lead 6297907524, EM 6304117632) were posted against `7a41253fcb` and are
spent: the head has moved twice since, first for the fix commit and then for
the rebase onto `develop`. Every finding of both reviews is answered finding
by finding in the PR comments, and the PR body is rewritten because the
history it told was inverted. The queue needs a review pass on
`f0335113a3` that leaves its findings on the PR, so the review-coverage gate
resolves against the current head. The author does not carry that.

**Why the change exists.** The chat route read the session lock from one
artefact and the model allowlist from another, so a tenant that curated a
model list while its matched deployment had none fell through to the
unchecked `x-digi-model` branch. The loader merge is now the only place the
two config sources are reconciled, and the route reads one artefact: the
request's tenant on the embed surface, the deployment config on the session
surface. The new tests fail 7 times against `develop` without the PR and
exactly 3 times against the PR's first commit - the 3 being the review
findings.

Follow-up from DIG-4744 (DevOps Lead): this batch's `changes requested` verdict on digithings #6107 (scope @`9efe5ed308`) also holds PR #6149, which is stacked on #6107's branch and carries its two commits.

#6107 has no live owner ticket left - DIG-4782 was cancelled as superseded by this batch, and this batch is closed - so as merge captain the ask is to route its two blockers to a seat: the stale pool prose at `apps/digiquant/src/digiquant/research/docs/agentic/ARCHITECTURE.md:631` and `:633`, and the audit trail for the Gemini removal.

When they land on `chore/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`, #6149 rebases onto that head, local-ci re-runs on the new head, QA posts `Review verdict: APPROVE <new sha>` on that exact head, and only then is #6149 marked ready for the merge queue. The same note is on #6107's thread (comment 6312162531) and on DIG-4744.

## Batch addendum — one PR merged after the batch closed

digithings #6009 (DIG-4588) merged into develop at 08:50:48Z through the develop merge queue (merge commit `8faf228e56f8fcca77231a826359e22e9ba73a01`), ten minutes after this batch posted its approval on that head (PR comment 6311782617). The batch summary above says "0 merged in this batch", which was true when it was written: the merge landed afterwards.

Leaf DIG-4588 is closed as merged. The other ten verdicts in this batch stand exactly as posted, and the batch is closed.

## Close note

`dt-close-guard DIG-4881` first came back BLOCKED on the durability gate with "NO REMOTE CONFIGURED in /Users/chrisstefan/digithings-books/.paperclip/worktrees/DIG-4881-pr-review-batch-daily — this repo has no place its work can land". That is the run workspace, not the work: this batch carries no code, its whole product is the comments on this issue and the verdict comments on the eleven PRs, all of them pushed. Re-run with the durability gate skipped — `dt-close-guard DIG-4881 --no-durability` — gives "OK: safe to close (status=in_progress, pending human_only=0)", so the gate that matters here, DIG-924's pending human-only card, is clear.

Two corrections to what the summary above says:

- DIG-4608 was already `done` when this batch read it, after #6055 merged at 08:32; the batch did not move that leaf, it only recorded the merge.
- DIG-4863 (the independent-verdict ticket for #6145) was first cancelled as superseded, then corrected to `done`. It is the recorded blocker on DIG-4795, and Paperclip resolves a blocker only when it is done — with it cancelled, DIG-4795 stayed `blocked` and every status change on it came back 409 "Issue follow-up blocked by unresolved blockers". Its own brief says "post the verdict on the PR and on this ticket, then close this ticket", and the independent verdict exists (QA Lead, 07:30 on the ticket and 08:25 on the PR at head `555223d7190d`).

## What the batch changed

- Eleven PRs reviewed and verdicted on the PR itself, at the head named in each verdict: 8 approved (in-session marker + verdict marker + provenance marker), 3 changes requested (verdict marker only, no label and no in-session marker, so the queue keeps holding them).
- One of the eight approvals moved the queue: #6009 (DIG-4588) went from blocked to **queued** for merge. The other seven are still held by something a review cannot fix — #5964 and #6018 are CONFLICTING, #6133, #6142 and #6145 have no local-ci report, #6135's local-ci is pending, #6134's red local-ci is the measured host-runner flake.
- DIG-4613 back to `todo` for Backend Engineer, Core Services with the findings on it. DIG-4795 back to `in_review` — reviewed and approved, waiting to merge. DIG-4782 and DIG-4783 cancelled as superseded by this batch.
- #6113's failing `pr-title` check fixed on the same PR (the title now carries the `root` scope), so local-ci reports the review gate and nothing else.

Nothing in this batch needs Chris: no promotion, no merge into `main`, no spend, no client repo write. The develop merges are the launchd merge queue's job and they are already moving.

## Dispositions

- The eight approvals are marked ready here. The merge queue takes each one as soon as local-ci is green and the merge state is CLEAN — no card, no merge ticket, no per-PR issue.
- All eight are still held by something a review cannot fix: #5964 and #6018 are CONFLICTING (base moved) with green CI; #6009, #6133, #6142 and #6145 have no local-ci report; #6135's local-ci is pending; #6134's red local-ci is a measured host-runner contention flake, not the change. A rebase moves the head, so an approval is re-issued against the new head. The leaves stay in_review until the PR merges.
- #431 goes back to todo for Backend Engineer, Core Services with the findings on the leaf.
- The two per-PR review tickets of this batch, DIG-4782 (#6107) and DIG-4783 (#6113), are cancelled as superseded by this batch; their findings live on the PRs.
- #6055 (DIG-4608) merged through the queue at 08:32 today, before this batch opened; its leaf is moved to done.
- Not in this batch: the develop PRs whose leaves are todo, blocked or in_progress (#5994, #6016, #5581, #5441, #6102, #6105, #6146, #6147, #6149 and the theme drafts). Their standing changes_requested verdicts stay where they are, and each PR comes back when it has a new head to review.

Review verdict: changes requested — twelve-x #431 (DIG-4613) @ `e4173c5cbb5c`

The verdict from the 02:48 review stands at this head, and this batch does not override it. Blocker: `refresh_session_token.sh:123` echoes the unknown argument to stderr, which leaks the desk session token on the path the runbook uses. The finding from the 20 Oct round also still stands: the new dry-run CLI contract reached only 3 of at least 5 places that carry it — `session_catchup.yml:101` and `:404`, `scripts/confirm_feed_published.py:813`, `docs/PRIMEMARKET_DESK_API.md:556` and `.env.example:52` still tell a human to run the script in the form that now writes nothing.

Full findings on the PR (comment 6311786531, digithings-ai/twelve-x/pull/431#issuecomment-6311786531).

Leaf DIG-4613 is back to `todo` for Backend Engineer, Core Services (84d0c55c) with the findings on it.

Disposition: changes requested. No label and no in-session marker, so the queue keeps holding the PR.

Review verdict: changes requested — digithings #6113 (DIG-4783) @ `219512c310bc`

The verdict from the 04:35 review stands at this head, and this batch does not override it. One blocker: the guard is inert in the lane that spends the money — `conftest.py:114` only runs `pytest_configure` when pytest loads the repo-root conftest, and `digillm/pyproject.toml:51` carries `[tool.pytest.ini_options]`, so a run rooted in `digillm/` never loads it (measured: `pytest digillm/tests --collect-only` collected 0 of 308 tests, `cd digillm && pytest -m unit --collect-only` collected 0 of 272 unit tests, and `digisearch/tests` behaves the same). `digillm/src/digillm/client.py` is the spend-capable package and `.github/workflows/test-digillm.yml:52` runs `uv run --frozen --no-sync pytest digillm/tests`, so the guard has to load there.

Full findings on the PR (comment 6311786048, digithings-ai/digithings/pull/6113#issuecomment-6311786048).

Leaf DIG-4783 is the per-PR review ticket for this PR: it is cancelled as superseded by this batch, and the findings stay on the PR.

Disposition: changes requested. No label and no in-session marker, so the queue keeps holding the PR; the PR is a draft, so the queue would not pick it up in any case. The failing `pr-title` check on this same PR is fixed (the title now carries the `root` scope), so local-ci reports the review gate and nothing else.

Review verdict: changes requested — digithings #6107 (DIG-4782) @ `9efe5ed3084f`

The verdict from the 04:35 review stands at this head, and this batch does not override it. Two blockers: `apps/digiquant/src/digiquant/research/docs/agentic/ARCHITECTURE.md:631` still contradicts the rewritten pool table (it names deepseek-v4-flash and gemini-3.7-flash) and claims a CI workflow, `.github/workflows/validate-digiquant-pools.yml`, that does not exist in the tree; line 633 is stale the same way, with the master digest pinned to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash while `config/model_modes.yaml` carries 1017. The PR's "Documentation Updated" box is ticked for that file, so the documentation is inside the scope of the change.

Full findings on the PR (comment 6311785591, digithings-ai/digithings/pull/6107#issuecomment-6311785591).

Leaf DIG-4782 is the per-PR review ticket for this PR: it is cancelled as superseded by this batch, and the findings stay on the PR.

Disposition: changes requested. No `reviewed:agent` label and no in-session marker — that pair is the coverage hatch for a pass that found nothing to change — so the queue keeps holding the PR. The PR is a draft, so the queue would not pick it up in any case; the fix belongs to the author and the PR comes back to the next batch with a new head.

Review verdict: approve — digithings #6145 (DIG-4795) @ `555223d7190d`

The independent QA Lead verdict at this exact head stands, and I checked the fix myself: the gate now reads the commit's `authoredDate` instead of `committedDate` (`_commit_times` became `_author_dates`), a commit with no author date is left out rather than dated from the field a rewrite moves, and the three new tests are in the suite at this head — a rebased commit is attributed to its author and not to the rebasing seat, a rebase outside every run window still leaves the PR reviewable, and a commit with no author date is attributed to nobody. That is the blocking finding the earlier verdict named, closed and pinned.

Full findings on the PR (comment 6311785138, digithings-ai/digithings/pull/6145#issuecomment-6311785138).

Leaf DIG-4795 moves back to `in_review`: the review is done and the PR is waiting to merge, so the leaf waits with it.

Disposition: approved at this head, marked ready in this batch. Not a blocker, but keep in view: the gate refuses a PR it cannot attribute, and 9 of the 31 open develop PRs name no DIG ticket at all, so this PR still needs its ticket and trailer to stay mergeable once the gate enforces. The gate ships in shadow, so nothing is blocked by it today.

Review verdict: approve — digithings #6142 (DIG-4794) @ `4ded7180e519`

The round-2 blocking finding is closed in this head: `_resolve_woodpecker_repo_id` resolves the repository name against the Woodpecker API and refuses when it cannot, instead of falling back to the static id, and the by-name URL is built from the resolved base, so a real build is no longer refused by a 404 from a malformed path. The same commit redacts credentials from the logged target URL, parses `export KEY=value`, handles a non-UTF-8 config and re-reads its own log lines from the file. The round-2 reviewer verified the fix commit: 168 and 260 tests pass, ruff clean, secret-scan clean, python3.9 loads, by-name and by-id both read build 6#318. This PR carried no verdict marker, so the batch adds one at the current head.

Full findings on the PR (comment 6311784731, digithings-ai/digithings/pull/6142#issuecomment-6311784731).

Review verdict: approve — digithings #6009 (DIG-4588) @ `84a660142003`

I read the whole diff at this head: the retry loop exports its schedule (7 attempts, delays 0/2/4/8/12/15/15 s), a 30 s per-attempt abort cap and a 100 s overall budget; the abort timer is armed before the fetch and cleared in `finally`, so no path leaks it; transient is 5xx|429|408 and every other status fails fast. The last two commits make the no-response guard reachable at runtime (the catch no longer continues past it) and correct the note: the abort cap is a cap (`min(cap, budget left)`), and the never-answers case breaks at exactly 100,000 ms. Note, tests and code agree on the arithmetic.

Full findings on the PR (comment 6311782617, digithings-ai/digithings/pull/6009#issuecomment-6311782617).

Disposition: approved, marked ready in this batch. local-ci has not reported on this head. Non-blocking note for the request owner: the 100 s exchange budget plus digigraph's ~250 s run is ~350 s against the chat route's 300 s maxDuration.

I read the diff at this head: the publish workflow's multi-line `tags<<EOF` heredoc plus the new test that pins it (23 tests passed at f64e8cef6). The earlier approval named the pre-fix head `37d36f70737a`, so this is a fresh approval bound to the head the PR stands at now.

The owner rebases on the current develop; the merge state is CONFLICTING (81 commits behind), so the rebase moves the head and the approval is re-issued against the new head. Under the author-independence gate that ships with #6145 this PR also carries a commit outside every run window, so it would read as unverifiable once that gate enforces — the owner should bring that commit inside a run window on DIG-4505 when rebasing.

### What the gates read

The merge queue is the single authority on review coverage — `review-applied` is an ignored check. The queue reads the `reviewed:agent` label together with a comment carrying the literal `<!-- in-session-review -->`, and it takes the newest readable `<!-- opencode-power-pack:code-review verdict=... scope=@<sha> -->` marker as the verdict. Each verdict in this batch therefore lands on the PR itself, with the in-session marker, the verdict marker scoped at the head, and a provenance marker (`agent=`, `run=`, `head=`) that names the current head and the seat that wrote it. Coverage and verdict are two different reads: a verdict that lives only in this issue would leave every PR blocked with "no review pass left comments".

### Two things a reader of this batch needs to know

1. Every approval here is bound to the head named in it. All eight are still held by something a review cannot fix: #5964 and #6018 are CONFLICTING (base moved) with green CI, #6009, #6133, #6142 and #6145 have no local-ci report, #6135's local-ci is pending, and #6134's red local-ci is a measured host-runner contention flake (npm ci killed esbuild in the shared scratch worktree), not the change. The owner rebases or waits; a rebase moves the head and the approval is re-issued against the new head.
2. The three changes-requested PRs keep a standing blocking verdict, so the queue holds them. #6107 and #6113 are drafts — the queue would not pick them up in any case — and their per-PR review tickets are cancelled as superseded by this batch. #431 goes back to todo for its developer with the findings on the leaf.
